newsitem.title: UK: Russian seaborne crude exports fall in Nov-Petrak.
newsitem.headline: Russian seaborne crude exports fall in Nov-Petrak.

text.p: Russian seaborne crude exports fell about four percent in November as lower shipments from Black Sea ports more than cancelled out higher volumes from Ventspils in the Baltic, shipping inspectors Petrak said on Tuesday.

Crude exports from the four ports totalled 1.168 million barrels per day (bpd), nearly 50,000 bpd fewer than in October and a similar shortfall on the average for the first 11 months of the 1996, Petrak said.

Russia's leading Black Sea port of Novorossiisk shipped 621,877 bpd in November against 693,436 bpd in October, a 10 percent fall caused mainly by an 86-hour shutdown for pipeline maintenance and weather-related disruption.
Odessa shipped 127,408 bpd, down 36,000 bpd on October, while Tuapse saw exports fall to 93,988 bpd from 106,332 bpd.
November exports from the Latvian Baltic port of Ventspils totalled 324,798 bpd, up sharply from October's 253,084 bpd, and the second highest volume for the year so far, Petrak said.
